ranking_by: share of dry air by volume
title: The 5 Most Common Gases in the Air, Ranked (Oxygen Is NOT #1)

scenes.text: The five most common gases in the air you are breathing right now. Oxygen is not number one.

scenes.label: Neon · 0.0018%
scenes.text: Number five: neon. Just eighteen parts per million, the gas that glows red in signs.

scenes.label: Carbon dioxide · ~0.04%
scenes.text: Number four: carbon dioxide. About zero point zero four percent of the air, tiny, yet it still warms the planet.

scenes.label: Argon · 0.93%
scenes.text: Number three: argon. Almost one percent of the air, a gas that barely reacts, used inside light bulbs.

scenes.label: Oxygen · 21%
scenes.text: Number two: oxygen. About twenty-one percent of the air, the gas you need, yet barely a fifth of it.

scenes.label: Nitrogen · 78%
scenes.text: Number one: nitrogen. About seventy-eight percent of dry air, nearly four in every five molecules you inhale.

description:
The five most common gases in dry air, ranked by share of volume.
From neon to nitrogen, which makes up about seventy-eight percent, while the oxygen you need is only about twenty-one.
Did you think oxygen would be number one?
first_comment: Did you guess oxygen at number one? And what should we rank next?
